mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate over the past 3 months (measured as the change in FEDFUNDS from t-3mo to t) is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as a lower policy rate compresses discount rates and increases equity valuations.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are not significantly positive in periods where FEDFUNDS has declined over the past 3 months (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.5%, the S&P 500 tends to produce negative 20-day returns, reflecting the market's anticipation of reduced economic growth and increased risk aversion during monetary tightening.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are not significantly negative in periods where FEDFUNDS > 4.5% (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4.0% and housing starts (HOUST) exceed 800,000 units, the S&P 500 tends to have positive 20-day returns, indicating a strong labor market and robust housing demand that supports economic expansion and equity valuations.
regime_hint: strong labor market and housing demand
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are not significantly positive in periods meeting the condition (UNRATE < 4.0 AND HOUST > 800) (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During monetary tightening cycles (defined by FEDFUNDS > 4.0% and CPIAUCSL > 3.0%), the S&P 500 tends to produce negative 60-day returns, as higher interest rates and inflationary pressures reduce equity valuations and increase risk aversion.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are not significantly negative in periods meeting the condition (FEDFUNDS > 4.0 AND CPIAUCSL > 3.0) (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) fall below 700,000 units, the S&P 500 tends to have negative 60-day returns, reflecting a slowdown in the housing sector that signals weakening economic demand and reduced corporate earnings growth.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are not significantly negative in periods where HOUST < 700 (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) falls below 95, the S&P 500 tends to produce negative 60-day returns, indicating a contraction in manufacturing output that signals economic slowdown and reduced corporate profitability.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are not significantly negative in periods where INDPRO < 95 (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeds 5.0%, the S&P 500 tends to have negative 5-day returns, reflecting market concerns about economic weakness and reduced consumer spending that depress equity valuations.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are not significantly negative in periods where UNRATE > 5.0 (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When GDP growth (GDPC1) is below 1.0% and inflation (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 3.0%, the S&P 500 tends to have negative 60-day returns, indicating a 'stagflation' scenario that reduces corporate earnings and increases risk aversion.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are not significantly negative in periods meeting the condition (GDPC1 < 1.0 AND CPIAUCSL > 3.0) (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.
